name: Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma
aliases: Spinal Cord Lipoma of the Conus

criteria.description: Identification of a lipomatous mass involving the conus medullaris on MRI
Presence of neurological deficits consistent with conus medullaris syndrome such as lower limb weakness or bladder dysfunction
Exclusion of other spinal cord tumors or lesions by imaging and clinical evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI evidence of lipoma involving the conus medullaris plus compatible neurological symptoms and exclusion of other spinal lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on MRI findings combined with clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Conus medullaris syndrome with bladder and bowel dysfunction
searchTerms: spinal cord end syndrome with bladder and bowel problems
conus medullaris dysfunction causing urinary and fecal issues
lower spinal cord syndrome affecting bladder and bowels

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lower limb sensory loss in saddle distribution
searchTerms: loss of sensation in inner thighs and buttocks
sensory loss in groin and inner legs

common.symptomName: Lower back pain localized to lumbosacral region
Gait disturbance due to motor impairment
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to motor issues
gait problems caused by muscle impairment

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in lower limbs

searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in lower limbs

occasional.symptomName: Sphincteric disturbances other than bladder dysfunction
searchTerms: problems controlling other sphincters besides bladder
difficulty with sphincter muscles other than bladder

occasional.symptomName: Localized cutaneous stigmata over lumbosacral region (e.g., hypertrichosis, lipoma)
searchTerms: skin marks over lower back like extra hair or fatty lumps
cutaneous signs such as hairy patches or lipomas on lower back
localized skin abnormalities on lumbosacral area

rare.symptomName: Hydromyelia or syringomyelia associated with lipoma
searchTerms: fluid-filled spinal cord cavities with fatty tumors
spinal cord cysts linked to lipomas
hydromyelia or syrinx with spinal lipoma

imaging: MRI demonstrating a fatty mass contiguous with the conus medullaris
T1-weighted hyperintense lesion on spinal MRI consistent with lipoma
Absence of enhancement on contrast MRI differentiating from neoplastic lesions
other: Possible cutaneous markers such as subcutaneous lipomas or hypertrichosis overlying the lesion

distinguishingFeatures: Tethered cord syndrome may present similarly but lacks a discrete lipomatous mass on imaging
Often associated with thickened filum terminale rather than a conus lipoma
Ependymomas typically enhance with contrast on MRI
Usually present as intramedullary tumors without fatty components

redFlags: Rapid progression of lower limb weakness
Sudden onset of bladder retention or incontinence
Development of severe neuropathic pain or spasticity
references: Tekkök IH, et al. Spinal cord lipomas: clinical features and surgical management. Neurosurg Rev. 2001.
